name: Alan Auerbach
current_role: Founder, Chairman, CEO and President, Puma Biotechnology (NASDAQ: PBYI)
profile: Biomedical engineer turned biotech analyst turned founder. He founded Cougar Biotechnology in 2003, whose prostate-cancer drug abiraterone (Zytiga) led to J&J's ~$1bn acquisition in 2009, then founded Puma Biotechnology in 2010, which commercialises the breast-cancer drug neratinib (Nerlynx).
interesting_fact: Cougar's lead drug abiraterone acetate, licensed in as an early-stage asset, was approved for metastatic prostate cancer in the US in April 2011 after J&J bought Cougar in 2009.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding Cougar he was a biotech sell-side analyst (Wells Fargo Securities, Seidler Companies) and was ranked second in the NASDAQ/Starmine survey of analyst stock-picking performance in biotechnology; earlier he designed oncology clinical trials at Diagnostic Products Corp. He holds BS/MS degrees in biomedical engineering (Boston University, USC).
notes: Best route is via Puma IR (Mariann Ohanesian, Senior Director IR). Biotech focus, limited overlap with energy/data centers.

name: Xie Yi
current_role: Chairman, CEO and controlling shareholder, Suzhou Tianmai Thermal Technology (SZSE: 301626)
profile: Xie Yi founded Suzhou Tianmai in 2007 with his wife Shen Fenghua; it makes thermal-management parts (heat pipes, vapor chambers, synthetic graphite films) for customers such as CATL, Huawei and Samsung. The company listed in Shenzhen in 2024 raising $87m; he directly owns ~40.8% and in 2026 the company was issuing convertible bonds to expand.
interesting_fact: He started his first job at 16 at a local factory making thermal-management products, the same niche he later built a billionaire-scale company in.
notes: Low public profile, no English-language interviews found. Thermal management for electronics/batteries is relevant to data-center cooling. Reach via the securities affairs office (zq@ email from the 2026 half-year report); Chinese-language outreach advisable.

name: Yu Lili
current_role: Director, Changsha Jingjia Microelectronics (SZSE: 300474); stepped down as vice chair in Aug 2024
profile: Yu Lili (b. 1968) is a co-founding shareholder and long-time leader of Jingjia Microelectronics, the Changsha company best known as one of China's first domestic GPU designers (JM-series chips), listed in Shenzhen in 2016. Her husband Zeng Wanhui is chairman; she remains a board director, and the company is now pushing into GPGPU and edge-AI SoC chips.
interesting_fact: Jingjia is one of China's pioneering home-grown GPU makers; in 2025 its subsidiary launched the CH37 edge-AI SoC rated at 64 TOPS (INT8), extending it from graphics into AI compute.
deep_cut_fact: Per Jingjia's 2025 annual report, she has a high-school education and from 1988 to 2006 worked as manager of a Guangzhou auto-parts trading business and then deputy office director at Beijing Xinshenjian Economic & Technology Development Co. before taking a leadership role in the group in 2006.
notes: Very private, non-executive director; no interviews found. Chairman Zeng Wanhui (her husband) is the company's public face. Jingjia's GPU/AI-chip work is relevant to data-center themes, but it has strong defence-sector ties. Chinese-language outreach via board secretary office.

name: Deepak Mehta
current_role: Chairman (long-time CMD), Deepak Nitrite Ltd and its subsidiary Deepak Phenolics
profile: Deepak C. Mehta, a University of Bombay science graduate, has spent ~45+ years at Deepak Nitrite, founded by his father Chimanlal Mehta in 1970. He turned it from a nitrite maker into a diversified chemicals group with ~100 products and India's leading phenol/acetone producer; son Maulik Mehta is now CEO. He is active in FICCI and ICC on chemical-park policy.
interesting_fact: He was named among EY Entrepreneur of the Year (India) 2020 winners; Deepak Nitrite is a leading producer of phenol and acetone in India with 700+ customers worldwide.
deep_cut_fact: Per EY, the idea for the big phenol/acetone plant (Deepak Phenolics) came while he was scouting acquisitions in Europe and noticed European firms wanting to buy into India for growth, which convinced him to build at scale at home instead.
notes: IR contact is Company Secretary Arvind Bajpai. Son Maulik Mehta (CEO) is more visible in media and may be an easier route; company is investing heavily in petrochemical capacity in Gujarat.

name: Denis Frolov
current_role: Major shareholder/co-owner, Astra Group (MOEX: ASTR, Astra Linux); co-founder of Varton group
profile: Denis Frolov bought 80% of NPO RusBITech, developer of the Astra Linux operating system, in 2017; it became Astra Group, which IPO'd on the Moscow Exchange in 2023 and supplies software to the Russian state as Western vendors exited. He also co-founded lighting/electronics group Varton (mid-2000s), has stakes in Sistematika and Baikal Electronics, and dairy interests.
interesting_fact: After Astra's 2023 IPO he was reported as only the second Russian to become a dollar billionaire from software, after Eugene Kaspersky.
deep_cut_fact: A Higher School of Economics graduate, he spent about seven years at dairy maker Wimm-Bill-Dann, rising from investment analyst to development director, before moving into tech.
notes: Russia-based; Astra serves the Russian government and defence-linked customers, so check sanctions/compliance before any outreach. Very low public profile. Contacts come from 2023 press releases and may be outdated; astra.ru was not reachable from here.

name: Hou Juncheng
current_role: Chairman and controlling shareholder, Proya Cosmetics (SSE: 603605)
profile: Hou Juncheng, from Yueqing in Wenzhou, moved from auto repair into cosmetics wholesale in Yiwu, then co-founded the Proya brand with his brother-in-law Fang Yuyou in the early 2000s. Proya, listed in Shanghai, grew via lower-tier-city stores and later e-commerce into one of China's top domestic skincare groups; Hou remains chairman after Fang left management in 2024.
interesting_fact: Proya's core consumers are young women aged 18-24 in China's small and medium cities, a 'lower-tier' strategy that let a domestic brand outgrow many foreign rivals.
deep_cut_fact: In the 1980s he learned auto-repair from his brother-in-law and opened his own garage, which earned his first capital; when he noticed the cosmetics his relative sold all came from Yiwu, he handed off the garage and moved there to become a leading cosmetics wholesaler.
notes: Low-profile; rarely gives interviews. Route via board secretary Xue Xia (proyazq@ email, per H1 2026 report). Chinese-language outreach advisable; consumer-goods focus with little energy/data-center overlap.

name: Cyrus Madon
current_role: Executive Vice Chair, Brookfield Asset Management; Executive Chair, Brookfield Private Equity
profile: Queen's University commerce grad and CPA who began in corporate finance and recovery at PwC, then joined Brookfield in 1998 as CFO of its real-estate brokerage. He built and ran Brookfield's private equity group (Brookfield Business Partners) for years and is now executive vice chair of the ~$1tn asset manager. He sits on the C.D. Howe Institute board.
interesting_fact: As head of Brookfield's private equity arm he led its first-ever nuclear investment: buying Westinghouse out of bankruptcy from Toshiba for $4.6bn in 2018, later sold to Brookfield Renewable and Cameco (2022-23).
deep_cut_fact: On selling Westinghouse to the Brookfield Renewable/Cameco consortium he said: "Westinghouse is an exceptionally well-run business today and has a great future." He first joined Brookfield in 1998 as CFO of its real-estate brokerage business, not an investing role.
notes: Strong fit for an energy/data-center podcast: Westinghouse nuclear deal, and Brookfield is a major renewables and AI-infrastructure investor. Low personal media profile; route via Brookfield North America press office.

name: Patokh Chodiev
current_role: Co-founder and co-owner, Eurasian Resources Group (ERG); founder, International Chodiev Foundation
profile: Uzbek-born, Belgian-naturalised businessman who studied international law and Japanese at MGIMO and worked on Soviet-Japanese commercial relations in Tokyo. With Alexander Machkevich and Alijan Ibragimov ('The Trio') he built ENRC in Kazakhstan, floated it in London in 2007 and took it private in 2013; it is now ERG, a mining, smelting and energy group active in 14 countries.
interesting_fact: He speaks fluent Japanese and received Japan's Order of the Rising Sun in 2020 for developing Japan-Russia economic and cultural ties.
deep_cut_fact: In 2011 he acquired the Kubota Collection, 104 kimono by textile artist Itchiku Kubota made with the revived 'tsujigahana' dyeing technique, and his foundation has since toured it to Kazakhstan, Russia, Europe and North America, with key pieces shown at the Tokyo National Museum in 2020.
notes: Significant reputational and due-diligence considerations: ENRC/ERG has been the subject of long-running investigations, he appears in the Pandora/Panama Papers reporting, and he was involved in the Belgian 'Kazakhgate' affair. Review before featuring. Best route is the foundation (ICF), which is PR-active; ERG (erg.kz) has its own press office.

name: Hou Xiaodi
current_role: Founder and CEO, Bot Auto (Houston-based autonomous trucking company)
profile: Xiaodi Hou co-founded autonomous-trucking company TuSimple in 2015 and served as its CTO and then CEO, taking it public on Nasdaq in 2021 (the source of his Hurun listing). After leaving in 2022 he founded Bot Auto in Houston in 2023, which in 2025 ran what it called the first fully humanless commercial freight runs on Texas highways (Houston-Dallas, Houston-San Antonio).
interesting_fact: Bot Auto completed a commercial freight run with nobody in the cab and no remote driver; Hou framed it as 'a business, not a demonstration.'
deep_cut_fact: Before trucks he was a vision scientist: his 2014 Caltech PhD, advised by neuroscientist Christof Koch, modelled how humans pick out foreground objects and proposed 'Image Signature', an extremely fast algorithm for predicting where people's eyes land in an image.
notes: Open to media and very relevant (AI, autonomy, logistics). Ongoing litigation with TuSimple (now CreateAI) over IP and its liquidation; avoid as a topic. Hurun wealth figure dates from 2021 TuSimple valuation and is likely far lower now.

name: Chang Byung-gyu
current_role: Founder and Chairman of the Board, KRAFTON Inc. (KRX: 259960)
profile: KAIST-trained serial entrepreneur who co-founded Neowiz in 1997 (as CTO), started search engine First Snow, then founded Bluehole Studio in 2007, which became KRAFTON, maker of PUBG: Battlegrounds. KRAFTON listed in Seoul in 2021. He also founded seed VC BonAngels (2012) and chaired Korea's Presidential Committee on the 4th Industrial Revolution (2017-2020).
interesting_fact: PUBG set a world record in 2017 with $100m in pre-release sales in 79 days; Tencent's 2018 investment of over $500m for ~10% made the company a unicorn overnight.
deep_cut_fact: After leaving Neowiz in 2005 he founded First Snow (Cheotnun), a search-engine startup whose technology was sold to Naver/NHN in 2006 for ₩35bn (~$31m), money that seeded Bluehole the next year.
notes: Outspoken on Korean startup policy and entrepreneurship; gives speeches (e.g., Oct 2026 Korea Times coverage urging founders to leave comfort zones), making him a good podcast fit on the entrepreneurship angle. No published direct email found; go via KRAFTON corporate communications/IR.

name: Shoji Uehara
current_role: Honorary Chairman (Chairman Emeritus), Taisho Pharmaceutical; President, Uehara Memorial Foundation (last reported)
profile: Born Dec 1927, he joined Taisho Pharmaceutical (maker of Lipovitan D energy drink) in 1948, became president in 1973 and handed over to son-in-law Akira Uehara in 1982, becoming honorary chairman. The family took Taisho private in a ~$5bn management buyout in 2024. No death notice was found, but he would be about 98.
interesting_fact: His adoptive father Shokichi Uehara built Taisho into a household name and also served as a Japanese senator and head of the Science and Technology Agency.
deep_cut_fact: An art collector, he founded the Uehara Buddhist Art Museum in Shimoda (1983) and the Uehara Museum of Modern Art (2000), merged in 2017 as the Uehara Museum of Art, and wrote a book about his collection, 'Eiga ni Miserarete' (Captivated by Painting).
notes: Very elderly (b. 1927); alive status unconfirmed. Not a realistic podcast guest; if relevant, current Taisho leadership (Shigeru Uehara) is the active figure. Not on rich lists since 2020.

name: Nikolaus
current_role: Shareholder and shareholders' committee member, Knauf Group (Gebr. Knauf KG), Iphofen; retired from management in 2008
profile: Nikolaus Wilhelm Knauf (b. 1936), eldest son of Knauf co-founder Alfons Knauf, ran the family plasterboard/building-materials group with his cousin Baldwin Knauf from 1969 to 2008, overseeing technology while it expanded across Europe, Russia and the CIS. Knauf, still 100% family-owned, now has ~€15bn revenue and ~41,000 staff; the next generation (Alexander Knauf) leads it.
interesting_fact: Under Nikolaus and Baldwin, Knauf grew from a regional German gypsum works founded in 1932 on the Moselle into a global group with ~€15bn sales, while remaining entirely family-owned.
deep_cut_fact: Inside the company he led the technical side while his cousin handled administration; the pair received high Austrian state honours for opening up the southeast European market via Knauf's Austrian subsidiary after 1989. He also serves as a CSU councillor in Markt Einersheim near Iphofen.
notes: Name in input is just 'Nikolaus' (shared with Knauf, Baldwin), identified as Nikolaus Knauf. Aged ~90 and no longer in management. He was Russia's honorary consul in Nuremberg until March 2022; Knauf's Russia business was a source of controversy. Route via Knauf Group Corporate Communications (head Matthias Link).

name: Nathaniel Charles Jacob Rothschild
profile: Jacob Rothschild, 4th Baron Rothschild, founder of RIT Capital Partners, died in London on 26 February 2024 aged 87.
notes: Deceased (26 Feb 2024; source ITV News). His title passed to his son Nathaniel, 5th Baron Rothschild. RIT Capital Partners continues as a listed investment trust.

name: Trevor R Milton
current_role: CEO, SyberJet Aircraft (Utah business-jet maker developing the SJ30 and SJ36)
profile: Utah-born founder of Nikola Motor (2015), the hydrogen/battery-electric truck maker that went public via SPAC in 2020; he resigned that year, was convicted of securities fraud in 2022 and received a presidential pardon in March 2025. Nikola went bankrupt in 2025. He joined the group that bought SyberJet in 2024 and became its CEO, leading the nine-seat SJ36 light jet and seeking ~$1bn for AI-assisted aircraft.
interesting_fact: After his 2025 pardon he resurfaced as CEO of SyberJet, which selected the Williams FJ44-4 engine for its new SJ36 light jet in October 2025.
deep_cut_fact: Before Nikola he built dHybrid Systems (2012), which made natural-gas storage systems for heavy trucks and was acquired by Worthington Industries, the same company that later wrote Nikola's first $2m cheque.
notes: High reputational risk: convicted of fraud over Nikola statements (2022), pardoned 2025; SEC civil case dropped Sept 2025; past misconduct allegations (denied). Very media-active. The 2021-22 Hurun $1bn figure is stale. Route via SyberJet press.

name: Robyn Denholm
current_role: Chair of the Board, Tesla, Inc. (since Nov 2018); board member, Blackbird Ventures
profile: Sydney-born accountant and tech executive (Arthur Andersen, Toyota Australia, Sun Microsystems, CFO of Juniper Networks, briefly CFO of Telstra) who has chaired Tesla since 2018. Her wealth comes largely from Tesla stock options. She founded TreeArc Investment Group in 2021, chaired the Technology Council of Australia and led Australia's 2025 Strategic Examination of R&D.
interesting_fact: She chaired the Australian government's 2025 Strategic Examination of Research and Development, a national review of how Australia funds and runs R&D.
deep_cut_fact: Through her TreeArc Investment Group (founded 2021) she holds majority ownership of NBL basketball team the Sydney Kings, the Sydney Flames and the Women's National Basketball League; early on she spent about seven years in finance at Toyota Motor Corporation Australia.
notes: Strong fit (EVs, Tesla Energy/Megapacks, Australian tech ecosystem). Board can be contacted via Tesla's Corporate Secretary (ir.tesla.com FAQ). Australian channels (Sydney Kings, Blackbird, Australian tech/R&D policy) may be warmer routes than Tesla.

name: Deepak Kumar Seth
current_role: Founder and Non-Executive Chairman, Pearl Global Industries Ltd (NSE: PGIL); Non-Executive Chairman, PDS Ltd
profile: A St. Stephen's College, Delhi alumnus, Deepak Seth founded what became Pearl Global (formerly House of Pearl Fashions) and built it into one of India's largest listed apparel exporters and supply-chain groups, with ~25 factories in India, Bangladesh, Vietnam, Indonesia and Guatemala supplying Gap, Ralph Lauren, PVH, Inditex and Primark. Sons Pulkit and Pallak Seth now run Pearl Global and PDS respectively.
interesting_fact: Pearl Global makes ~84 million garments a year (FY24) with 30,000+ workers across five manufacturing countries, targeting 120-140 million pieces by FY28.
deep_cut_fact: The company began in 1987 with a single export order for 6,000 shirts; from there he set out to build a fully integrated garment maker when most Indian exporters were small tailoring units or merchant traders.
notes: Low personal media profile; the sons (Pulkit Seth, MD of Pearl Global; Pallak Seth, PDS) are more visible. IR head is Shishir Gahoi. Country blank in input; he is Indian (Delhi/Gurugram based).

name: Rob Sands
current_role: Director, Constellation Brands (NYSE: STZ); former CEO (2007-2019) and Executive/Non-Executive Chair (2019-2023)
profile: Robert Sands, second-generation leader of Constellation Brands (founded by his grandfather as a regional wine company), was CEO 2007-2019 and chair until 2023. With his brother Richard he turned it into an S&P 500 beverage-alcohol group (Corona, Modelo, Robert Mondavi) with $9bn+ revenue; he led the acquisition of the US rights to Grupo Modelo's Mexican beers and the build-out of its Mexican breweries. He remains a board director.
interesting_fact: As CEO he led the 2013 acquisition of the US business for Corona and Modelo and the build-out of Constellation's own Mexican brewing footprint, which made it the top US beer importer.
deep_cut_fact: Before running the business he was its lawyer: he served as Constellation's General Counsel from 1986 to 2000, overlapping with his rise to EVP and CEO of the international unit.
notes: Input had only a Wikidata ID (Q52004979); matches Robert Sands of Constellation Brands (director since 1990, age 67 in 2026 proxy). corpsecretary@ is the published route for contacting board members. Constellation is investing heavily in water/energy for its Mexican breweries, a possible energy angle.

name: Udo Mueller
current_role: Founder and CEO (sole CEO again since April 2026), Ströer SE & Co. KGaA, Cologne
profile: Udo Müller co-founded Ströer City Marketing in 1990 with outdoor-advertising pioneer Heinz Ströer (50/50) and built it into Germany's largest out-of-home media group, listed in 2010, adding billboard networks (DSM, Deutsche Eisenbahn-Reklame) and digital assets such as t-online.de. He holds ~22-23% and in 2026 returned to sole leadership as Ströer pushes into AI and digital out-of-home.
interesting_fact: Ströer, which started from billboard advertising, bought news portal t-online.de and digital marketer InteractiveMedia from Deutsche Telekom in 2015 for about €300m, turning an outdoor advertiser into one of Germany's biggest online publishers.
deep_cut_fact: Ströer's 1990 origin was a 50/50 joint venture, Ströer City Marketing, between Müller and Heinz 'Heiner' Ströer, who had run an outdoor-ad business since 1964; that JV became Ströer Out-of-Home Media AG in 2002.
notes: Co-CEO Christian Schmalzl's structure was dissolved in April 2026 (Horizont), so Müller is sole CEO. German-language outreach via Ströer press office is best. Some limited energy angle via digital-screen power use; mainly a media/adtech story.
